To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

circulating levels of endothelial microparticle are inversely correlated with endothelial function and are associated with the severity of coronary artery disease in patients with ischemically impaired LV function.

the number of circulating endothelial microparticle (EMP) correlates inversely with endothelium-dependent coronary vasodilation and that the number of EMP is increased in patients with chronic ischemic heart disease.
the number of circulating endothelial microparticle in patients with ischemia-induced left ventricular dysfunction correlates with endothelial function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of circulating microparticles and endothelial function in heart failure.
the role of the endothelium in cardiovascular disease.
the study of the effects of atherosclerosis on endothelial function in the coronary and peripheral circulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

there are no clear and consistent associations between the levels of circulating endothelial microparticle levels and the presence of cardiovascular risk factors, the presence of atherosclerotic lesions or the presence of a clinical cardiovascular event.
endothelial function in the human body is a complex phenomenon and that the assessment of the endothelial function is not a simple task.
the endothelium is a dynamic organ that is constantly exposed to various stimuli, both physiological and pathophysiological.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
endothelial microparticle (EMP) release is a marker of endothelial dysfunction.

endothelial dysfunction and inflammation are associated with atherosclerosis and that these processes can be measured by circulating endothelial microparticle (EMP) counts and by the expression of adhesion molecules.
we have identified a new class of biomarkers for the detection of cardiovascular disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
endothelial microparticle levels are inversely related with endothelial function and are elevated in patients with ischemia-induced left ventricular dysfunction.
we found a novel mechanism by which the immune system can contribute to the development of atherosclerosis.

endothelial microparticle (EMP) levels are associated with endothelial function and may be a potential biomarker for cardiovascular disease in patients with left ventricular dysfunction and ischemic heart disease.
